newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Sinopec plans to float seven firms by 2000.
newsitem.headline: China's Sinopec plans to float seven firms by 2000.

text.p: China Petrochemical Corp (Sinopec), China's state-owned oil firm, plans to float seven of its companies overseas by the end of the decade, the South China Morning Post said on Saturday.
The group would float enterprises that had good business performance, the newspaper quoted its president Sheng Huaren as saying.

The candidates were Beijing Yanshan Petrochemical Co, Yangzi Petrochemical Co, Jinling Petrochemical, Qilu Petrochemical Co, Liaoyang Petrochemical Fibre Co, Maoming Petrochemical Co, and Daqing General Petrochemical Works.
Yanshan and Yangzi could be the front-runners, Sheng added.
"We will select only one or two companies per year for issuing shares abroad," he was quoted as saying.
Sinopec, with 38 refinery and petrochemical offshoots, has already listed Shanghai Petrochemical Co Ltd and Zhenhai Refining and Chemical Co Ltd.
Company officials were not immediately available for comment.
